items.title: The fibres of the canonical morphism to the spectrum of global functions are geometrically connected
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k with A = H^0(X, O_X), the lemma shows that the fibres of the canonical morphism X to Spec(A) are geometrically connected (statement lines 2012-2017). The proof first identifies A as a finite product of local Artinian k-algebras A_i finite over k, so that Spec(A) is the disjoint union of the singletons Spec(A_i) (proof lines 2020-2026), then reduces to an algebraically closed base field by base changing to the algebraic closure and using that the cohomology of the structure sheaf is preserved under flat base change (proof lines 2028-2052). In the algebraically closed case the argument is a clean local-ring computation: with X_i the inverse image of Spec(A_i), one has A_i = Gamma(X_i, O_{X_i}); if the fibre were disconnected then X_i would be disconnected, giving a nontrivial idempotent in the local ring A_i, a contradiction (proof lines 2054-2071). The claim is H2: standard inputs, but the reduction to the algebraically closed case and the idempotent argument are both written out and the local structure of A is what drives the proof.
